name: aq_project_status
description: Overview of the open AnimaQuill project: its name, frame rate, picture formats and languages; each timeline with its length and its numbers of tracks and clips; its scenes, sounds, assets and shared code files (up to 30 of each; aq_search finds the rest); whether it can be changed; and how many problems it has. It does not list clips or keyframes: those are in aq_timeline_read and aq_object_read. Like every result, it starts with the project revision; the tools keep track of revisions themselves, so no call needs it back.

name: aq_timeline_read
description: What is on one timeline: one compact line per clip, sorted by start, with its id, name, track, start..end in seconds, what it shows (asset=, scene=, sound=, color=, text=), the transitions at its edges, its effects, and how many properties it sets and how many of them are animated. The result also lists the sections the timeline is made of, its tracks from the back of the picture forward, joins (transitions between two clips that touch) and markers. from and to (seconds) and tracks narrow it; cursor pages through long timelines; without timeline it reads the first timeline of the project. It has no property values or keyframes: every field of a clip is in aq_object_read. The clips it lists count as read for the conflict check of aq_edit.

timeline.description: Timeline id, as aq_project_status lists it. Without it, the first timeline of the project.

from.description: Only clips that end after this moment. Seconds as a string, such as "12.5".

to.description: Only clips that start before this moment. Seconds as a string, such as "12.5".

tracks.description: Only clips on these tracks, by track id.

limit.description: How many clips at most, 1 to 500; 200 by default.

cursor.description: Where to go on, as the last line of an earlier result of this call says.

name: aq_object_read
description: Objects of the project by id, with every field as the project format writes it: clips with their source, transitions, effects, properties and keyframes; tracks, sections, joins, markers, scenes, sounds, assets, timelines, or "project" for the project settings. The JSON has the same shape that aq_edit operations take. fields (dotted paths such as "properties.transform.x" or "effects") limits the result to those fields. For a clip that shows a scene, it also lists the properties the scene describes, with their type, unit, range and default; these are the paths property.edit takes. Clip ids are unique only within a timeline; timeline picks one when several timelines have the same id. Up to 20 objects per call; response_format "concise" gives one line per object and a summary of its top-level fields instead of the full JSON.

ids.description: Ids of clips, tracks, sections, joins, markers, scenes, sounds, assets or timelines, or "project", 1 to 20.

timeline.description: Timeline id, for ids that several timelines have.

fields.description: Dotted paths to read only these fields, such as "start", "properties.transform.x" or "effects".

response_format.description: "detailed" (the default) gives every field as JSON; "concise" one line per object and its top-level fields.

name: aq_search
description: Finds objects in the project by id, name, kind or text: clips that show a given asset or scene, tracks, markers, scenes, sounds, assets, files by path, and text inside the code of scenes and sounds (kind "text" answers with path:line and the line). Matching ignores case and finds the query anywhere in the id, name, path or source. Without query it lists everything of the given kinds. Results are compact lines with ids that the other tools take.

query.description: Text to find, any case, in ids, names, paths, sources, or the text of code files (kind text).

kinds.description: Only these kinds of objects; every kind but text by default.

timeline.description: Only objects of this timeline, by its id.

limit.description: How many results at most, 1 to 200; 50 by default.

cursor.description: Where to go on, as the last line of an earlier result of this call says.

name: aq_file_read
description: A code file of the project: the HTML, CSS and JavaScript of a scene (under scenes/<id>/), the code of a sound (under sounds/<id>/), or shared code (under code/). Lines come numbered as "   12→text"; the numbers are not part of the file. offset (the first line) and limit (how many lines) read a long file in parts. aq_file_write replaces an existing file only if all its lines were read here in this conversation. Project settings, timelines, scenes' manifests and assets are not files here: they are in aq_object_read.

path.description: Path of a code file, such as "scenes/title/index.html", as aq_project_status or aq_search lists it.

offset.description: The first line to read, from 1; 1 by default.

limit.description: How many lines at most, 1 to 2000; 2000 by default.

name: aq_selection_read
description: What the user is pointing at in the editor right now: the timeline they are on, the playhead time, the current version, the selected clips (ids and one line each) and the selected transition. It has only what the user chose to share; the full objects are in aq_object_read.

name: aq_guide
description: The AnimaQuill manual: a reference page for every operation of aq_edit (topic "ops/<operation>", such as "ops/property.edit": parameters, what it returns, its errors and examples), the project format (topics "format/…": times, ids, world coordinates, clips, transitions, effects, properties and keyframes), and how scene code talks to the editor (topics "scene-runtime/…"). Without arguments it gives the table of contents; topic gives one page; query searches the titles and text by keywords.

topic.description: One page, such as "ops/clip.move", "format/animaquill.json" or "scene-runtime/aq"; ":2" after it for its next part. Without topic and query, the table of contents.

query.description: Words to look for in titles and pages; it gives up to 10 topics, each with a line of what it says.

name: aq_edit
description:
Changes the open project with a batch of operations — the same operations the editor's own commands use — on timelines, sections, tracks, clips, transitions, joins, effects, properties and keyframes, markers, scenes, sounds and assets. It does not change the text of code files; aq_file_edit and aq_file_write do. scene.add and sound.add take the first files of a new scene or sound. All operations of one call succeed together or nothing is written, and the batch is one step the user can undo. Operations run in order, so a later one can refer to an object that an earlier one created with an id given in the batch, such as "clip_title2". Times are strings in seconds, such as "12.5" or "1001/30000"; positions and sizes are in world units, with the origin at the center of the picture. Ids of existing objects come from the reading tools; an id that does not exist fails with not-found. Changes are checked against what you have read: a change to an object that the user changed after you last read it fails with conflict, and a change to an existing object before anything was read in this conversation fails with not-read; in both cases nothing is written. dry_run: true checks the batch and reports everything it would change or remove, including what uses those objects, without writing. A failed call says which operation failed, why, the correct shape and an example. The result lists the objects that changed, the ids of new objects, and the problems this batch introduced or resolved. summary is one short sentence that the user sees for this batch, saying what it does. Operations (every parameter, result and more examples: aq_guide topic "ops/"): project.rename {name} — rename the project project.setFrameRate {fps} — set the frame rate the timeline counts frames by asset.update {asset, changes:{name?, tags?:[string]}} — rename an asset or change its tags asset.remove {asset, withUses?} — remove an asset, and with withUses the clips that use it scene.add {id?, manifest, files:object} — create a scene (HTML, CSS and JavaScript that draw a picture) with its files scene.update {scene, changes:object, clear?:["description"|"params"|"presets"|"tags"]} — change the manifest of a scene: name, entry, params, presets scene.remove {scene, withUses?} — remove a scene and its files, and with withUses the clips that use it sound.add {id?, manifest, files:object} — create a sound made by code, with its files sound.update {sound, changes:object, clear?:["description"|"params"|"outputs"|"tags"]} — change the manifest of a sound: name, entry, params, outputs sound.remove {sound, withUses?} — remove a sound and its files, and with withUses the clips that use it source.replace {kind, from, to} — make every clip that uses an asset, scene or sound use another one of the same kind clip.add {timeline, track, name?, start, duration, source, offset?, loop?, enter?, exit?, hidden?, draft?, link?, sectionFit?, properties?:object, effects?:[{id, type, enabled?, start?, end?}], id?, overlap?} — put a clip on a track: an asset, a scene, a sound, a color or a caption clip.remove {timeline, clips:[string]} — remove clips clip.update {timeline, clip, changes:{name?, source?, offset?, loop?, hidden?, draft?, link?, sectionFit?}, clear?:["name"|"offset"|"loop"|"hidden"|"draft"|"link"|"sectionFit"]} — change the name, source, offset, loop, hidden, draft, link or section fit of a clip clip.move {timeline, clips:[{clip, start?, track?}], overlap?} — move clips to other starts or tracks, in one step clip.trim {timeline, clip, start?, end?} — move the start or end of a clip; what it shows stays in place clip.split {timeline, clip, at, piece?, keep?:[string]} — cut a clip in two at a moment of the timeline file.remove {path} — remove a code file that is no entry file.rename {from, to} — rename or move a code file timeline.rename {timeline, name} — rename a timeline section.add {timeline, id?, duration, name?, before?} — add a section to a timeline, which makes it longer section.update {timeline, section, duration?, name?} — change the duration or name of a section section.remove {timeline, section} — remove a section; a timeline keeps at least one track.add {timeline, id?, kind, name?, before?} — add a video, audio or caption track track.update {timeline, track, changes:{name?, locked?, group?, hidden?, muted?, solo?, role?}} — change the name, hidden, muted, solo, locked, group or role of a track track.move {timeline, track, before?} — move a track before another one, or last track.remove {timeline, track} — remove a track with all its clips clip.setTransition {timeline, clip, enter?, exit?} — put a transition at the start (enter) or end (exit) of a clip, or take it away with null join.add {type?, transition?, library?, resource?, duration?, curve?, values?:object, timeline, id?, from, to, align?} — put a transition on the cut between two clips that touch join.update {timeline, join, changes:{type?, transition?, library?, resource?, duration?, curve?, values?, align?}} — change the type, duration, align, curve or values of a join join.remove {timeline, joins:[string]} — remove joins effect.add {timeline, clip, id?, type, enabled?, index?, values?:object, start?, end?} — put an effect on a clip, with the values of its parameters effect.remove {timeline, clip, effects:[string]} — take effects off a clip effect.move {timeline, clip, effect, index} — move an effect in the list of its clip, which changes what it works on effect.update {timeline, clip, effect, enabled?, start?, end?} — turn an effect on or off, or change when it works property.edit {timeline, edits:[PropertyEdit]} — set properties of clips and their keyframes, in one step property.rename {timeline, renames:[PropertyRename]} — give properties of a clip another path, with their keyframes, after code renamed what they are about marker.add {timeline, id?, time, name?, note?, color?, duration?} — add a marker to a timeline marker.update {timeline, marker, changes:{time?, name?, note?, color?, duration?}} — change the time, name, note, color or duration of a marker marker.remove {timeline, marker} — remove a marker Examples of operations (illustrative; their ids come from a sample project, not from the open one): name: aq_file_edit
description: Changes part of a code file by replacing exact text: each edit's old_text must appear exactly once in the file as it is now (without the line numbers that aq_file_read shows), and is replaced with new_text; replace_all replaces every occurrence instead. All edits of one call apply in order and succeed together, or nothing is written. It does not use the file's revision, so the user's edits elsewhere in the same file do not stop it; old_text that is not found is not in the file as it is now, as when that part changed after it was read. The file must exist: aq_file_write creates files. The result shows the changed lines and a syntax check.

path.description: Path of the code file, such as "scenes/title/index.html".

old_text.description: Text of the file as it is now, exactly, without the line numbers of aq_file_read; enough of it to be found once.

replace_all.description: true replaces every place old_text is found, at least one.

request_id.description: Any string of yours: a call sent again with the same one is not run again and gets the same result.

name: aq_file_write
description: Creates a code file or replaces all of one. Paths go under scenes/<scene id>/, sounds/<sound id>/ or code/, and the scene or sound must exist (scene.add and sound.add in aq_edit create them with their first files). An existing file is replaced only if all its lines were read with aq_file_read in this conversation, and the call fails with file-changed if somebody changed it since. Replacing a whole file also replaces any edits the user made elsewhere in it; aq_file_edit changes only the parts it names. The result includes a syntax check.

path.description: Path of the file, under scenes/<scene id>/, sounds/<sound id>/ or code/, such as "code/ease.js".

base_revision.description: Hardly ever needed: a revision from an earlier result, to also refuse the write if the file changed since then. The file still has to be read first.

request_id.description: Any string of yours: a call sent again with the same one is not run again and gets the same result.

name: aq_propose
description: Hands a decision to the user: kind "question" shows the question with 2 to 6 short options, and the user can also answer in their own words. The turn ends with this call: changes later in the same answer are not run, and the answer arrives as the user's next message.

kind.description: "question": a choice for the user to make.

question.description: The question, in one sentence, in the language of the user.

label.description: A short answer the user can pick.

detail.description: What picking it means, in a few words.

allow_other.description: false when the user must pick one of the options; by default they can also answer in their own words.

name: aq_check_run
description: Lists the problems of the project: files that do not fit the project format, references to things that are missing, values that do not fit what a scene describes, errors that scene and sound code threw when the editor ran it, and things this editor version does not do yet (they do not appear in the preview or the export). Runtime errors come only from code the editor has run: a scene runs while one of its clips is in the preview, and again after its code changes; the result lists changed code that has not run since. aq_edit results already include the problems that come from the project data alone. A fix line is an aq_edit operation that resolves that problem.

checks.description: "format": whether every document fits the project format; "problems": all problems the editor knows of. Both by default.

subject.description: Only problems of this object id or file path.

limit.description: How many problems at most, 1 to 500; 100 by default.

cursor.description: Where to go on, as the last line of an earlier result of this call says.
